from.place: the sheafification step: use the universal property of sheaf tensor

title: Universal property of sheaf tensor product
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathrm{Bilin}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G,\mathcal H)$ be the set of morphisms of sheaves of sets $\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ that are $\mathcal O(U)$-bilinear on sections over every $U$. Composition with the morphism $\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] induced by pure tensors gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G,\mathcal H)\cong\mathrm{Bilin}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G,\mathcal H)$, natural in $\mathcal H$.

proof.text: For each object U of the site, the ordinary module tensor-product universal property identifies O(U)-bilinear maps F(U) \times G(U) \to H(U) with O(U)-linear maps F(U) \otimes_{O(U)} G(U) \to H(U). Compatibility with restriction maps is preserved in both directions, so these sectionwise bijections identify O-bilinear morphisms F \times G \to H with morphisms of presheaves of O-modules F \otimes_{p,O} G \to H. The presheaf tensor product is sectionwise the indicated module tensor product by [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Section 03EK, characterization of the presheaf tensor product by bilinear maps

proof.text: Since H is already a sheaf of O-modules, the universal property of module sheafification gives a bijection between morphisms of presheaves of O-modules F \otimes_{p,O} G \to H and morphisms of sheaves of O-modules (F \otimes_{p,O} G)^# \to H: every presheaf morphism factors uniquely through the sheafification. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], (F \otimes_{p,O} G)^# is F \otimes_O G.

source.place: Section 03EK, sheafification step after the presheaf tensor product

proof.text: Composing the bijections of the preceding two steps yields a bijection Hom_O(F \otimes_O G,H) \cong Bilin_O(F \times G,H). Under this bijection a morphism is sent to its composite with the canonical pure-tensor morphism F \times G \to F \otimes_O G, and the inverse sends a bilinear morphism to the unique sheaf morphism induced by its sectionwise tensor maps. Thus the displayed bijection has exactly the asserted meaning.

The ordinary module tensor-product bijections commute with restriction and with postcomposition in H, and the sheafification factorization is unique and functorial in the target sheaf. Therefore the composite bijection is natural in H.
